scope: Targeted code crawl and bug bash of access/file boundaries, transfers, queue persistence/recovery, CLI crash recovery, shared desktop input, and release packaging. Three audit agents assisted; root integrated and reviewed the changes.

actual: Disposable HTTP servers and file-integrity checks
Clean npm/portable installations and native terminal startup
mocked: Windows platform branching; actual Windows execution not performed
Native mobile bridge and browser DOM/pointer events
Provider/app delivery and helper pipe events
not_validated: Live provider messages or actual desktop typing/clicking

findings.finding: Binary downloads could read outside a share after a checked pathname was replaced by a symlink.
findings.evidence_before: Both authenticated and short-lived-link routes served replacement bytes in four deterministic filesystem-swap regressions.
findings.fix: Open and validate the file once, then stream from that FileHandle; preserve ranges, conditional requests, hidden-file policy, and link identity checks.

findings.finding: An upload could publish outside its share if its destination folder changed during asynchronous preparation.
findings.evidence_before: Swapping incoming for an outside-directory symlink during truncate created notes.txt outside the shared root.
findings.fix: Reauthorize and re-resolve the destination after preparation and before publication; reject changes and retain the upload for retry.
findings.limit: This closes the reproduced asynchronous preparation gap. It does not provide descriptor-relative directory operations or claim to eliminate syscall-level parent-directory races after the final path check.

findings.finding: Uploads failed if Reach restarted between successful chunks or after receiving all bytes but before completion.
findings.evidence_before: Both new restart-timing tests reached failed instead of done; completion incorrectly claimed the destination folder was gone.
findings.fix: Recreate lost sessions and resend from byte zero, bounded to two renewals. Stop on revoked access, missing folders, or conflicting destination names.

findings.finding: An already-disconnected chunk body could leave its upload session stuck indefinitely.
findings.evidence_before: A destroyed stream whose close event had already fired never settled until the regression explicitly released it.
findings.fix: Reject destroyed request bodies before allocating a file writer. Also normalize copy-fallback EEXIST internally; HTTP already mapped that code to 409.

findings.finding: Native download cancellation/setup races could leave tasks running, leak listeners, or leave canceled transfers marked running.
findings.evidence_before: All three mocked mobile-bridge regressions failed before the change: late task allocation was never canceled, listener setup escaped cleanup, and native cancellation left running state.
findings.fix: Register cancellation before awaiting bridge setup, clean partial subscriptions, cancel tasks allocated after cancellation, and reflect native cancellation in the tray.

findings.finding: Failed queue edits remained eligible for delivery, and failed cancellation writes were acknowledged as successful.
findings.evidence_before: Injected storage failure retained rejected text in memory; a supposedly canceled message reappeared when the outbox was reopened.
findings.fix: Roll back rejected edits and make explicit cancellations durable before acknowledging them.

findings.finding: Removing a paused queue head could strand later messages; reordering ready messages did not wake the delivery worker.
findings.evidence_before: Both disposable mocked-provider regressions failed to deliver the ready message after the queue mutation.
findings.fix: Wake and resume delivery after successful cancellation or reordering.

findings.finding: Crash recovery retained restart -y and removed legitimate directory names such as restart.
findings.evidence_before: Both launchers failed dedicated restart-flag and folder-argument preservation regressions.
findings.fix: Consume only actual restart commands and their confirmation flags, preserving ordinary folder arguments.

findings.finding: Stopping during supervisor backoff retained a referenced timer, delaying process exit by up to 30 seconds.
findings.evidence_before: A real disposable Node subprocess retained one timeout after stop; after the change it retained zero.
findings.fix: Abort the backoff sleep when the supervisor is awakened or stopped.

findings.finding: UTF-8 split across helper pipe chunks corrupted clipboard/selection text and agent replies.
findings.evidence_before: Both desktop readers turned split Cafe-with-accent data into replacement characters. New tests split multilingual/emoji replies at every byte boundary.
findings.fix: Use a streaming StringDecoder in both shared helper readers.

findings.finding: Middle and extra mouse buttons generated primary remote clicks.
findings.evidence_before: The UI regression observed left-click actions after buttons 1, 3, and 4.
findings.fix: Begin primary pointer gestures only for button zero, preserving separate context-menu handling.

findings.finding: The older-iOS AbortSignal.any fallback retained listeners from completed requests on long-lived view signals.
findings.evidence_before: Both cancellation and already-aborted-input regressions observed a remaining listener instead of zero.
findings.fix: Remove every source listener when the combined signal aborts, preserving its reason and deduplicating sources.

findings.finding: The history secret scanner treated two historical extension public keys as generic API secrets.
findings.evidence_before: Gitleaks flagged two manifest.key values; crypto.createPublicKey parsed each as a DER SPKI RSA public key.
findings.fix: Exclude only the two exact immutable finding fingerprints. All other scanner rules/findings remain active.

verification.server_batch_resolution: The one failing Windows fixture inherited REACH_COMMAND=reach from the parent Terminal. Its source-launcher fixture now resets that variable; all seven file tests passed on rerun. Other server cases were unchanged and were not needlessly repeated.
verification.counting: 210 server cases after the 7-case fixture rerun + 162 distinct client cases + 1 cleanup case (CI cases already counted in the server batch) + 34 service/guide cases = 407.
verification.packages: npm run package and npm run verify:package passed; npm and portable archives clean-installed outside checkout, with authenticated files, initial UI assets and native terminal smoke checks.
verification.release_privacy: node scripts/check-release.mjs passed; this is a guardrail rather than a guarantee of absence of all private data.
verification.guard: Every Node test ran through npm run test:file with test/helpers/runaway-guard.mjs. No full npm test was started.
verification.local_logs: reports/bug-bash-2026-10-16/ (ignored; raw failures and passing runs retained locally)

deployment.live_session: Original Terminal Reach left running; no start, stop, or restart performed.
deployment.server_fixes: Require an authorized CLI restart to become active.
deployment.ui_fixes: Release UI rebuilt; Reach handles interface reloads without a server restart.

workspace: Pre-existing credential-recovery edits and concurrent service/tool edits were preserved. The service/tool changes are included in validation but are not attributed as bug-bash fixes.
